items.followUp: State one advantage of wind energy and one advantage of geothermal energy.

rubric.why: Identifies the source of wind energy and how it is used.
rubric.description: Wind energy comes from moving air and can be used to turn turbines to generate electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying moving air as the source and 1 mark for stating that it turns turbines or generates electricity.

rubric.why: Identifies the source of geothermal energy and a use for it.
rubric.description: Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth, used for heating or generating electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heat inside the Earth as the source and 1 mark for stating a use, such as heating or generating electricity.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is obtained from moving air and can be used to turn turbines to generate electricity.
Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth; it can be used for heating or to generate electricity.

items.followUp: A force of 100 N acts at 60° to the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Uses the correct component relations for an angle measured from the horizontal.
rubric.description: The horizontal component is F cos θ and the vertical component is F sin θ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both correct component formulae.

rubric.why: Calculates the horizontal component using the force and angle.
rubric.description: The horizontal component is 200 cos 30° = 173.2 N (approximately).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for the correct value with unit.

rubric.why: Calculates the vertical component using the force and angle.
rubric.description: The vertical component is 200 sin 30° = 100 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for the correct value with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, θ = 30° to the horizontal road.
Horizontal component: Fx = F cos θ.
Vertical component: Fy = F sin θ.
The horizontal component is 173.2 N and the vertical component is 100 N.
